method: Verified all assigned file SHA-256 values against ROOT snapshot. Enumerated every unchecked key from S02.json, reviewed its full extracted task text and corresponding source line/context; checked JEV/toolkit references against the accepted typed-decision handoff and APP implementation. No task in this shard benefits from replacing measurement, deterministic verification, kernel code, or human authority with Jev: local typed choice primitives do not speed CPU/GPU kernels, establish performance, authorize a production change, or produce independent benchmark evidence. No JEV refinements proposed; therefore no APP API claim requires a proposed adapter. No inference/build/reload/process action. Reviewed the selection/judge and correctness-labeled items individually: typed decisions cannot replace exact numeric correctness or operator-owned measurement-grade changes. Source-only/fixture and existing-artifact replay work is separated from GPU/benchmark acceptance.

RVP-C6-21 explicitly re-scores the identical already-generated C6 corpus with and without the functionality/semantic tier, and says this needs no ground truth, GPU, or training. Implement/run the paired scorer over existing artifacts as offline replay and report the numeric gap; preserve the warning that the cited paper self-grades its own ≤3pp arm. This measures the grader’s marginal contribution, not a JEV confidence signal.

RVP-C6-22 closes a concrete dtype-downgrade escape: add required output and accumulation dtype per operator to the generated-kernel contract, then assert them structurally before selecting tolerance. Existing-source review and mutation fixtures can establish this without GPU execution; the typed-decision confidence value is not a precision oracle.

RVP-C6-23 is source adoption, not a new benchmark run: inspect FlashInfer-Bench `lowbit.py`/`default.py` at the pinned revision, extract actual `eps_abs`, `eps_rel`, and `rho`, then specify matched-ratio checks, NaN/Inf rejection, and maximum observed error in the C6 correctness contract. Validate the host comparator with synthetic tensors; no model/kernel benchmark is needed for this bounded slice.
